title: Structuring the Unstructured - Cedric Clyburn, Red Hat
talk_summary: A Red Hat engineer demos Docling, an open-source local document parser that converts PDFs/images/tables into structured markdown/JSON/Pydantic for RAG and agents, with a chunkless-RAG pattern and MCP/REST serving options. The core claim is that deterministic local layout-aware parsing beats naive PDF text extraction and expensive VLM calls for accuracy and cost.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic local document parsing before LLM ingestion
takeaways.what_they_do: Run Docling locally (CPU, no GPU) to convert PDFs/tables/images into structured markdown/JSON/Pydantic instead of dumping raw text or paying a VLM per document.
takeaways.evidence_quote: allowed him to do this at 50 times of a cost savings compared to VLMs and OCR naively
takeaways.numbers: ~50x cost savings vs naive VLM/OCR; runs on CPU

takeaways.what_they_do: Use the document's markdown section outline as the retrieval index; the LLM picks relevant sections and pulls full text, skipping chunker/embedding/vector DB.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're doing RAG but without having to use a chunker or embedding model or vector database
takeaways.numbers: 418-section annual report handled in an agentic loop

takeaways.technique: Docling MCP server for agent document ops
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose Docling conversion/generation/manipulation as MCP tools so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) can parse and manipulate documents agentically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also use the Docling MCP server ... give it the capabilities that Docling has through that model context protocol

takeaways.what_they_do: Run Docling as a containerized REST service (docling-serve) to batch-process hundreds/thousands of documents with per-request options (OCR, backend, image annotation).
takeaways.evidence_quote: deploy docling as a REST API service using something that's known as docling serve
